evidence.description: The task returns the decoded, filtered array, then invokes map with a closure that awaits MainActor.run.

candidates.explanation: The detached task returns an array of NewsModel values, so calling map on its value iterates over individual models rather than passing the complete array to the closure. The closure also contains await, making it asynchronous, but Array.map requires a synchronous closure. This restoration expression is not a valid asynchronous array transformation.
candidates.title: Invalid asynchronous use of Array.map

evidence.description: Initialization launches restoration in an unstructured task.
Loading independently launches another task and updates items after the network request.
Restoration replaces the entire item set rather than accounting for intervening updates.

candidates.explanation: Initialization starts restoration without exposing or awaiting its completion, while load can independently fetch and merge news. Restoration unconditionally replaces items. If restoration completes after a load has updated items, it can overwrite the newly fetched state with the older cached state.
candidates.title: Restoration can overwrite freshly loaded state

evidence.description: Each eligible invocation starts an independent load task that subsequently awaits save.
Save captures the current items and writes that snapshot to the shared file from a detached task.

candidates.explanation: Each load can start an independent save, and each save captures its own snapshot before writing in a detached task. MainActor isolation does not serialize these detached writes while callers are suspended. An older snapshot can finish writing after a newer snapshot and replace the cache with stale data; atomic writes prevent partial files, not out-of-order replacement.
candidates.title: Concurrent saves can persist stale snapshots

evidence.description: Decode failure returns silently, and the surrounding catch discards request errors.
Cache read and decode errors are converted into an empty result.
Persistence errors are caught and ignored.

candidates.explanation: Network, decoding, restoration, and persistence failures are discarded without reporting them to callers or recording diagnostic information. Callers cannot distinguish a failed refresh from a successful no-op, and a failed cache write remains invisible even though the in-memory state has already changed.
candidates.title: Operational failures are silently discarded
